div.head: ECf retr 37
div.ab: (Decretum regis) de usurariis. Usurarios quoque defendit rex Eadwardus, ne remaneret aliquis in toto regno suo; et si quis inde conuictus esset, quod fenus exigeret, omni substantia propria careret et pro exlege haberetur.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 668 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page; the words in bold are the Retractator’s changes to ECf, as Liebermann prints them.

note.seg: Eadward III., nach der Legende Verächter des Geldes, erscheint nirgends als Bekämpfer des Wuchers, ebensowenig wie Robert oder Heinrich I. von Frankreich, oder als häufiger Besucher letzterer. Um 1031 bezeugt Edward eine Urkunde Roberts von der Normandie neben König Heinrich, qui tunc profugus in hac terra; Round Cal. of doc. in France I n. 1422. — Kronrecht 12. Jahrhs. in Normandie und England confiscirte den nicht der Kirche legirten Nachlass der Wucherer; bei Lebzeiten aber strafte diese nur die Kirche; vgl. mein Über Edw. Conf. 38. 106; Madox Hist. Exchequer 237; Hughes Dial. de Scacc. by Rich. son of Nigel 224

Edward III, by the legend a despiser of money, nowhere appears as a fighter against usury, any more than Robert or Henry I of France do, nor as a frequent visitor of the latter. About 1031 Edward witnesses a charter of Robert of Normandy beside King Henry, qui tunc profugus in hac terra; Round, Cal. of doc. in France I no. 1422. — The crown law of the 12th century in Normandy and England confiscated usurers’ estates not bequeathed to the Church; but in their lifetime only the Church punished them; cf. my Über Edw. Conf. 38. 106; Madox, Hist. Exchequer 237; Hughes, Dial. de Scacc. by Rich. son of Nigel 224

div.ab: (Decree of the king) concerning usurers. King Edward also forbade usurers, that none should remain in his whole kingdom; and if anyone were convicted of it, [namely] that he exacted interest, he should be deprived of all his own substance and be held as an outlaw.
